editorial:
When Joseph Stalin suddenly drops dead, his closest advisors panic and start scheming for power. You watch a group of selfish, nervous men try to outsmart each other while pretending to care about the country. The vibe is dark but hilarious, mixing real history with sharp comedy that keeps you laughing even when things get tense. Every character feels like a real person, and the awkward situations they create are both funny and a little scary.

The acting is fantastic, especially Steve Buscemi as Nikita Khrushchev, who brings nervous energy to every scene. The pacing moves fast, so you never get bored, though the humor can feel a bit dry if you are not into political satire. If you enjoy smart, biting comedy, this is a great pick. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection. It is a fun watch for movie night with friends who like something different.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Khrushchev finally outmaneuvers his rivals and takes control of the Soviet Union. Beria is arrested and executed, while the others fall in line behind Khrushchev. The twist is that the man who seemed like a nervous sidekick all along was actually the most dangerous player. The movie ends with Khrushchev watching a concert, looking powerful but still uneasy, hinting that his victory may not last forever.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves sharp political comedy and history fans.
